module

public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Unique realization of odd primes $p \notin \{3, 5\}$ by continued fraction values

$a(n)$ is the denominator of the finite continued fraction
$$\frac{1}{2 - \frac{3}{3 - \frac{4}{4 - \frac{5}{\dots - \frac{n-1}{(n-1) - \frac{n}{n+4}}}}}}$$

*References:*
- [A372761](https://oeis.org/A372761)
- [arxiv/2605.22763](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.22763) *Advancing Mathematics Research with AI-Driven Formal Proof Search* by George Tsoukalas et al.
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace OeisA372761


open scoped Nat

open Rat

/--
Recursive helper computing the continued fraction denominator $R_k(n)$ for $2 \le k \le n-1$,
where $R_k(n) = k - \frac{k+1}{R_{k+1}(n)}$ with base case $R_{n-1}(n) = (n-1) - \frac{n}{n+4}$.
-/
def continuedFractionDenominator (n k : ℕ) : ℚ :=
  if n ≤ 2 then 0
  else
    if 2 ≤ k ∧ k ≤ n - 1 then
      if k = n - 1 then
        (k : ℚ) - (n : ℚ) / (n + 4 : ℚ)
      else
        let R_next := continuedFractionDenominator n (k + 1)
        if R_next = 0 then 0 else (k : ℚ) - (k + 1 : ℚ) / R_next
    else 0
termination_by n - k

/--
Denominator of the continued fraction
$$ \frac{1}{2 - \frac{3}{3 - \frac{4}{4 - \frac{5}{\dots - \frac{n-1}{(n-1) - \frac{n}{n+4}}}}}} $$
-/
def a (n : ℕ) : ℕ :=
  if n < 3 then 0 -- Sequence starts at n=3.
  else (1 / continuedFractionDenominator n 2).den


@[category test, AMS 11]
lemma a_3 : a 3 = 11 := by
  delta a; repeat rw [continuedFractionDenominator]; norm_num

@[category test, AMS 11]
lemma a_4 : a 4 = 4 := by
  delta a; repeat rw [continuedFractionDenominator]; norm_num

@[category test, AMS 11]
lemma a_5 : a 5 = 7 := by
  delta a; repeat rw [continuedFractionDenominator]; norm_num

@[category test, AMS 11]
lemma a_6 : a 6 = 13 := by
  delta a; repeat rw [continuedFractionDenominator]; norm_num

@[category test, AMS 11]
lemma a_7 : a 7 = 31 := by
  delta a; repeat rw [continuedFractionDenominator]; norm_num


/--
Conjecture: Except for 3 and 5, all odd primes appear in the sequence once. - _Thomas Scheuerle_, May 11 2024

A formal proof has been found with the methods described in
[arxiv/2605.22763](https://arxiv.org/abs/2605.22763).
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11, formal_proof using lean4 at
"https://github.com/mo271/formal-conjectures/blob/a32396489dcb8f86c3549b93aa358ac6a10a3a1f/FormalConjectures/OEIS/372761.wip.lean#L733"]
theorem exists_unique_a_eq_prime :
    ∀ p : ℕ, Nat.Prime p ∧ p % 2 = 1 ∧ p ≠ 3 ∧ p ≠ 5 → ∃! n, n ≥ 3 ∧ a n = p := by
    sorry

end OeisA372761

findings.description: The theorem docstring credits the conjecture to "_Thomas Scheuerle_, May 11 2024". In A372761 this is "Conjecture 2", and it was already in the sequence author's original submission (Mohammed Bouras, May 12 2024) with no attribution, so by OEIS convention it is Bouras's. Thomas Scheuerle never edited or commented on the entry. Also, the date May 11 2024 is before A372761 was even allocated (May 12 2024, 13:30 EDT). The Lean mathematics is unaffected: this is a reference slip only.
findings.source_evidence: OEIS internal format (oeis/oeisdata seq/A372/A372761.seq, current revision #16 and the earliest export #4 of May 31 2024): "%C A372761 Conjecture 2: Except for 3 and 5, all odd primes appear in the sequence once." (no attribution); "%A A372761 _Mohammed Bouras_, May 12 2024". Revision history (https://oeis.org/history?seq=A372761, read through a reader proxy): #1-#3 Mohammed Bouras (May 12 2024; #2 contains both conjectures), #4 and #7 N. J. A. Sloane, #5-#6 Bill McEachen, #8-#9 Michel Marcus, #10 and #13 Sean A. Irvine, #11-#12 Ralf Stephan, #14-#16 Michael De Vlieger. The name Scheuerle does not appear anywhere in the history. arXiv:2608.11941, Table (settled_conjectures_table.tex): "Conjecture (Mohammed Bouras, 2024). Every odd prime p∉{3,5} occurs as a term at exactly one index n≥3."
findings.suggested_fix: Replace the attribution with the author's, e.g. "Conjecture 2 of A372761: Except for 3 and 5, all odd primes appear in the sequence once. - _Mohammed Bouras_, May 12 2024", or drop the attribution.

reformulations.difference: The helper `continuedFractionDenominator` returns a default 0 whenever the next tail R_{k+1} is 0. That 0 then propagates, and since `1/0 = 0` and `(0:ℚ).den = 1`, it would make `a n = 1`. A true continued fraction with a vanishing tail is undefined instead. The AlphaProof Nexus file that OEIS links handles the edge cases differently: it has no guard on R_3 and treats n = 3 as a special case.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Downward induction on k shows R_k(n)·(k−1) > k(k−2) for all 2 ≤ k ≤ n−1 and n ≥ 3. Base: R_{n−1} = (n−1) − n/(n+4) > n−2. Step: if R_{k+1}·k > (k+1)(k−1), then R_{k+1} > 0 and (k − (k+1)/R_{k+1})(k−1) > k(k−2). So every tail is positive and no guard ever fires. Hence `continuedFractionDenominator` satisfies R_k = k − (k+1)/R_{k+1} with base R_{n−1} = (n−1) − n/(n+4), and `a n` is the reduced denominator of 1/(2−3/(3−…−n/(n+4))) for every n ≥ 3, i.e. exactly A372761. I proved this in Lean (`cfd_bound`, `cfd_pos`, `cfd_rec`, `cfd_base`; axioms propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound). I also proved `OeisA372761.a n = a_APN n` for all n. Numerically, `a` matches the b-file for n = 3..71 and the closed form IntQ2(n)/(2(5n−4)) for n ≤ 400.

reformulations.difference: The source says "Except for 3 and 5, all odd primes appear in the sequence once". The Lean states only the universal part: every odd prime p ∉ {3,5} occurs at exactly one index n ≥ 3. It says nothing about 3 and 5, which the word "except" might be read as calling genuine exceptions.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Under the plain reading, the Lean is literally the claim. This is also exactly how the OEIS editors (they record Conjecture 2 as proved by the AlphaProof Nexus Lean file, which has the identical statement) and arXiv:2608.11941 ("Every odd prime p∉{3,5} occurs as a term at exactly one index n≥3") state it. Under the stronger reading, the extra conjunct is a true fact, so the two readings are equivalent. 5 never occurs: an odd prime value p = a(n) divides 5n−4 (I proved `fc_a_ne_five` in Lean from the APN lemma). 3 never occurs: none for n ≤ 1500 by computation, and in general, when 3 | 5n−4 and n ≥ 6, v_3((n−1)(n−3)!(n+4)) ≥ v_3(5n−4), so the 3-part of the denominator cancels in IntQ2/(2(5n−4)). Small n were checked directly.

The claim itself was verified independently. I patched three Mathlib renames in the AlphaProof Nexus proof and compiled it here, and proved that its definition of `a` equals the FC definition for every n. That gives a proof, in my scratch file, of a theorem whose type is `type_of% @OeisA372761.exists_unique_a_eq_prime`, using only propext, Classical.choice and Quot.sound.
review.notes:
The mathematics of the file is faithful. The only defect is the misattributed conjecture in the theorem docstring (minor).

1. Definition check. A reviewer might worry that the default-value guards change the sequence. They cannot: every continued-fraction tail is positive (proved in Lean for all n), so `a` is exactly A372761. The tests `a_3`..`a_7` (11, 4, 7, 13, 31) match the OEIS data, and `a` equals the b-file for n = 3..71.

2. Statement check. `∀ p, Nat.Prime p ∧ p % 2 = 1 ∧ p ≠ 3 ∧ p ≠ 5 → ∃! n, n ≥ 3 ∧ a n = p` is Conjecture 2 with the sequence's offset 3. `a n = 0` for n < 3, so the `n ≥ 3` guard is harmless. Numerically, every odd prime p ≤ 397 other than 3 and 5 occurs exactly once among n ≤ 400; the proof's bound n < p+3 makes these counts complete. 2, 3 and 5 never occur for n ≤ 1500.

3. Status. `research solved` matches OEIS (Ralf Stephan, Jun 18 2026: \"Conjecture 2 was proved by an autonomous AI agent, see the Lean file\"; also arXiv:2608.11941 lists it as proved). No status issue.

The equivalence of the two definitions needed R_3(n) ≠ 0 for n ≥ 4. Where that fails, the FC `a` would give 1 and the APN `a` would give 2. My positivity lemma shows it never happens.
